title: OpenCode Model Routing — Fallback Chain Contract
description: Canonical schema for the per-agent routing fields consumed by both the Go writer (omr) and the TypeScript runtime plugin: the fallback chain and the blocked-models set. Both live under the OMR plugin tuple option at `plugin[N][1].agents.<name>.fallback_models` / `.blocked_models` inside OpenCode's global `opencode.json`. Legacy `agent.<name>.options.fallback_models` is read only for migration because OpenCode forwards `agent.options` into provider/model request options.

fallback_models.description: Ordered list of `provider/model` pairs to try in sequence when the primary model fails. Empty array == no fallback (single-model behavior).

items.description: A `provider/model` identifier. Consecutive dots (`..`) are rejected. Examples: `openai/gpt-5`, `google/gemini-2.5-pro`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`.

blocked_models.description: Exact `provider/model` keys the routing plugin must never select for this agent. A blocked current model is preemptively redirected to the first healthy non-blocked chain entry, and the fallback rotation skips blocked entries. Matching is exact-key only (no patterns). May list models outside the fallback chain.

items.description: A `provider/model` identifier. Consecutive dots (`..`) are rejected. Examples: `openai/gpt-5`, `google/gemini-2.5-pro`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`.

family_disjoint_from_parent.description: Per-agent opt-in for the model-family disjointness constraint. When true, a model selected for this agent must not share a model family with the model serving the requesting parent session. Intended for second-opinion sub-agents (e.g. `concord-advisor`): same-family verification carries systematic bias that is hard to detect downstream. Family comes from the global `model_families` map — never from the provider ID, which is not a family (`opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash` and `zai-coding-plan/glm-5.3` are two providers and one GLM family). A candidate with no `model_families` entry is skipped (disjointness must be proven, not assumed). When no chain rung satisfies the constraint, or the parent's model is unknown or unmapped, routing is unchanged and a warn event is emitted — the constraint never hard-fails a consult. Applies at every selection path: preemptive redirect, fallback rotation, availability preflight target selection, and suppressed-replay rung advance.

model_families.description: Global map of `provider/model` key → model family (e.g. `"zai-coding-plan/glm-5.3": "glm"`), read by the family_disjoint_from_parent constraint. Lives at the plugin tuple level beside `agents`, not per-agent. Entries whose key fails the model-key pattern or whose value is empty are dropped with a warning. This field is plugin-reader-owned: it has no Go writer and is deliberately absent from schema-contract-check.sh's FIELDS list.

router.description: Per-agent first-turn router designation (plugin tuple `agents.<name>.router`). Presence designates the agent: on the first chat.message of a child session dispatched to this agent, the prompt is graded low | medium | high | extreme and the grade selects `tiers.<grade>` — the ordered candidate list the router walks. A grade with no tier entry fails open to the agent's configured model. Only `tiers` is read; any other member is ignored.

tiers.description: Ordered candidate lists per grade. Each list is walked in order; the first candidate that passes model admission (cooldown, blocklist, availability veto, family veto), has no fresh zero-remaining quota boundary, and whose provider is below its provider_session_caps entry becomes the session's model.

provider_session_caps.description: Global map of providerID → maximum concurrent live sessions for the first-turn router (plugin tuple level, beside `agents`). Counts come from the host-wide live-session registry — one file per busy session across every OpenCode process on the host — so a new dispatch skips a provider already at its cap. Per provider because plan concurrency is per account. A candidate whose provider has no entry here is never cap-filtered.

jev.description: Jev classifier configuration (plugin tuple level). The OpenRouter API key is read from `api_key_file` at call time; it never travels through an environment variable. Absent or invalid config fails every routing decision open to the agent's configured model — no Jev call is made.

api_key_file.description: Path to a file holding the OpenRouter API key (leading `~/` is expanded). Trailing whitespace is trimmed.

routerTierList.description: Ordered `provider/model` candidate list for one router grade. Up to 8 entries, same key pattern as fallback_models.

$comment: Cross-stack consumers MUST reference the field names `fallback_models` and `blocked_models` verbatim. Drift between Go writer (internal/config/) and TS reader (plugin/src/) is enforced via schema-contract-check.sh in `make lint`. The `family_disjoint_from_parent` and `model_families` fields are TS-reader-owned (the Go writer neither reads nor writes them) and are intentionally not part of that cross-stack check.
